place_name: Manassas Junction / First Bull Run battlefield, Va.
note: Site of the First Battle of Bull Run (21 July 1861) -- fought while Elias's own 6th Ohio was away in the Cheat Mountain / Laurel Hill campaign in western Virginia, so he was not part of it. He passed directly through the site over a year later: his letter of 6 Nov. 1862 records, "We left Centerville on Sunday Morning camped at Manassas junction."

Site of the Battle of Fredericksburg (11-15 Dec. 1862). Elias's 75th Ohio was not engaged there, but camped six miles away days afterward. His letter of 19 Dec. 1862 (the transcript itself misheads it "/61"; content places it unambiguously in 1862) says: "We are now at Staffords C.H. 6 miles from Fredricksburgh from which place we have just arrived... there are thousands lying on the Battle field of Fredricksburgh who suffer more than tongues can tell."
